target: रोज़ थोड़ा पैदल चलना सेहत के लिए अच्छा है।
english: Walking a little every day is good for your health.
reason: Environmental-essay register — a textbook motto, not something anyone says. Replacement keeps the same infinitive-as-subject + के लिए अच्छा है pattern in everyday talk.

target: अनीता का आजकल काम में मन नहीं लग रहा।
english: Anita isn't able to focus on work these days.
reason: "अपना लोहा मनवाना" is a literary idiom a learner will never use, and this is a near-duplicate of hi-2649. Replacement teaches a genuinely common idiom (मन लगना) in the same subject + काम frame.

target: यह दुकान गाँव के कई लोगों को काम देती है।
english: This shop gives work to many people in the village.
reason: Development-report register, and "हथकरघा इंडस्ट्री" is an unnatural Hindi-English graft (spoken Hindi would be रोज़गार, not नौकरी देती है). Replacement keeps the same subject + को + देती है frame.

target: हमें बता दिया गया है कि सोमवार को ऑफ़िस बंद रहेगा।
english: We've been told that the office will be closed on Monday.
reason: "सूचित किया जाता है कि" is pure notice-board bureaucratese. Replacement keeps the passive + कि-clause but in the way a colleague would actually say it.

target: रोज़ सुबह चाय पीना मेरी पुरानी आदत है।
english: Drinking tea every morning is an old habit of mine.
reason: Culture-guide blurb — a learner will never need to state that bindis are an Indian tradition. Replacement keeps the same infinitive-subject + X है pattern with usable content.

target: मेहनती लड़के ने सारे सवाल ख़ुद हल किए।
english: The hardworking boy solved all the questions himself.
reason: School-essay writing ("पसीना बहाया" + मेहनती मज़दूर) rather than speech. Replacement keeps the adjective + ने-perfective structure in an ordinary situation.

target: इस दुकान पर सबसे अच्छी मिठाई बनाई जाती है।
english: The best sweets are made at this shop.
reason: Festival trivia in textbook register; no learner will say this. Replacement keeps the same habitual passive (किया/बनाई जाती है) with something you'd say while out shopping.

target: मेरे घर पहुँचते ही बारिश शुरू हो गई।
english: It started raining as soon as I got home.
reason: Theatre-review register; the -ते ही construction deserves an example from daily life. Replacement keeps -ते ही + perfective main clause.

target: मीटिंग रद्द होने की ख़बर सबको मिल गई।
english: Everyone got the news that the meeting was cancelled.
reason: Officialese ("स्थगित होने की सूचना... दे दी गई"). Replacement keeps the same verbal-noun + की + news/notice pattern in spoken register.

target: गेंद को दीवार के पार मत फेंको, वरना खो जाएगी।
english: Don't throw the ball over the wall, or it'll get lost.
reason: Unnatural — "चिड़िया को जाल के पार भेजो" is nobody's badminton Hindi (you'd say नेट के ऊपर से मारो). Replacement keeps को + के पार + imperative with everyday vocabulary.

target: इस मंदिर की दीवारों पर बनी तस्वीरें बहुत खूबसूरत हैं।
english: The paintings on this temple's walls are very beautiful.
reason: Tourist-guidebook trivia plus literary vocabulary (भित्ति चित्रण) a learner will never use or hear. Replacement keeps की + पर + adjective predicate with words that recur.

target: मीटिंग सोमवार सुबह दस बजे रखी जाएगी।
english: The meeting will be held at ten on Monday morning.
reason: Circular-notice register (प्रातः, आयोजित की जाएगी). Replacement keeps the future passive but with the words people actually use for scheduling.

target: वह दुबला-पतला ज़रूर है, पर बहुत ताक़तवर है।
english: He is thin, sure, but he's very strong.
reason: Storybook narration about an unnamed man — says nothing a learner would use. Replacement keeps the दुबला-पतला echo compound in a sentence you'd really say about someone.

target: कृपया समय पर ऑफ़िस पहुँचने की कोशिश करें।
english: Please try to reach the office on time.
reason: "प्रयास करें" + कार्यालय is written-notice Hindi; spoken Hindi is कोशिश करें + ऑफ़िस. Same oblique-infinitive + की + verb structure, natural register.

target: इस नल से पूरे घर में पानी आता है।
english: Water comes to the whole house from this tap.
reason: Geography-textbook sentence about canal irrigation. Replacement keeps the same से ... में + habitual present pattern in a household setting.

target: वह तकिये पर सिर रखकर तुरंत सो गया।
english: He put his head on the pillow and fell asleep right away.
reason: Subjectless novel-prose, and मखमली (velvet) is decorative vocabulary. Replacement keeps the -कर conjunctive participle with a stated subject and ordinary words.

target: मेरी आपसे गुज़ारिश है कि आप थोड़ा जल्दी आ जाएँ।
english: I'd request you to come a little early.
reason: Station-announcement officialese and a near-duplicate of hi-2959 (same यात्रियों से...है कि frame). Replacement keeps से ... है कि + subjunctive as a polite everyday request.

target: कोलकाता बहुत पुराना और खूबसूरत शहर है।
english: Kolkata is a very old and beautiful city.
reason: Encyclopedia entry — "ऐतिहासिक नगर" is written register (spoken is शहर). Replacement keeps the simple X है predicate with words a learner will reuse.

target: यह दुकान पूरे बाज़ार में सबसे पुरानी है।
english: This shop is the oldest in the whole market.
reason: Niche subject (the village flour mill) and awkward ordering. Replacement keeps the same सबसे + adjective superlative in a place a learner actually goes.

target: दुकानदार ने सारे सामान का बिल बना दिया।
english: The shopkeeper made out the bill for all the goods.
reason: सराफ़ is obscure trade vocabulary (and the English gloss is wrong — it's a jeweller, not a money changer). Replacement keeps the ने-perfective + का with everyday shop vocabulary.

target: इतनी लंबी बातचीत से कोई नतीजा नहीं निकला।
english: Nothing came of such a long conversation.
reason: Academic-report phrasing ("तुलनात्मक अध्ययन से नतीजे निकाले गए"). Replacement keeps से + नतीजा निकलना in the way it's actually said.

target: उसने कमरा साफ़ करके सारा सामान ठीक से रख दिया।
english: He cleaned the room and put everything away properly.
reason: Subjectless farming sentence with formal agricultural vocabulary (खरपतवार). Replacement keeps the -कर participle + साफ़ करना with a subject and household content.

target: तेज़ बारिश में सड़कें पानी से भर गईं।
english: The roads filled up with water in the heavy rain.
reason: Translationese — "सड़कें जम गईं" isn't how roads and ice are described in Hindi, and blizzards aren't a context these learners meet. Replacement keeps में + plural subject + compound verb.
